summary: Eikan Taki specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a member of Taisho University and served as a lecturer at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962–1966). From around 1989 to 2013, he served as a professor in the Faculty of Humanities and director at Taisho University.
Eiko Okukaze works in Buddhist studies. She studied as a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010) and has held a post as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Eileen Power (1889–1940) was a historian who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Paris. She held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). He has held posts at the JSPS (attested 2014), Kyoto University (attested 2015), and Koyasan University (attested 2014 and 2026).
Eisei Kojima worked in Buddhist studies. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at Ryukoku University and as the president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) studied Buddhist studies and Japanology at Rissho University (~1931–1936) under Gyoo Kageyama. He later held posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1949–1983).
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson (attested 1998).

Eivind Kahrs works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He has held positions at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2010) and served as a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eiyin Yasuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1957–1961) and trained under Gyōin Hashimoto.
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at institutions including Toyo University and Sera Monastery. He served as rector of Gohyaku Rakan-ji and became a professor at Toyo University in 1916.
Ekkyo Uno works in Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies at Columbia University (attested 2010) and joined the faculty at Stanford University (attested 2026).

Eleanor Nesbitt is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Oxford. Around 1989, she joined the University of Warwick, where she became an emerita professor in Education Studies.

Eleanor Rosch studied at Reed College and earned her Ph.D. under Roger Brown at Harvard University. A scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies, she held posts at Brown University and became a professor at UC Berkeley in 1971.

Elena Bashir specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1982–1988) and held positions at the University of Chicago beginning in 2000, including editorial board membership (attested 2026).
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian History under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome (~1967–1971), where she later became an associate professor in 1980.
Elena France Hanson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~2011–2014) and held a post there (2016–2017). In 2020, she became an assistant professor at the University of Groningen.
